title: Molecular Line Observations in Two Dusty Star-forming Galaxies at z = 6.9
question: What are the physical properties of the molecular interstellar medium, gas mass, CO-to-H2 conversion factor, gas depletion timescales, and heating mechanisms in the two dusty star-forming galaxies of SPT0311-58 at z = 6.9?

data.angular_resolution: ~0.5'' at 95 GHz, ~0.3'' at 140 GHz; continuum beams: 0.31'' x 0.22'' (Tuning 1), 0.47'' x 0.36'' (Tuning 2), 0.27'' x 0.20'' (Tuning 3)

what.value: ALMA B6, B7, B8 continuum flux densities, [CII] 240 GHz observations, and lens modeling magnifications

evidence.quote: The source has been observed in previous ALMA cycles (2015.1.00504.S, PI: Strandet and 2016.1.01293.S, PI: Marrone) in B3, B6, B7, and B8 corresponding to 95, 240, 340, and 420 GHz, respectively.
The intrinsic continuum flux densities (corrected for magnification) in W and E are obtained by performing lens modeling described in detail in (cite: marrone18).

Since the spectral lines are non-Gaussian and blended in the case of $\rm CO(7-6)$ and \[CI\]$\rm (2-1)$, and $\rm CO(10-9)$ and p-$\rm H_{2} O (3_{1,2}-2_{2,1})$, we use \[CII\] from the ALMA 240 GHz observations (cite: marrone18) as a template to derive the spectral properties.

what.value: ATCA CO(3-2) data reduction and line properties

evidence.quote: We include $\rm CO(3-2)$ data observed with ATCA to constrain the CO spectral line energy distribution (SLED). The data reduction and line properties are present in (cite: strandet17).
We also include *Herschel*/SPIRE photometry at 250, 350, and 500 $\mu$m (project ID: DDT$\_$mstrande$\_$1, (cite: strandet16)).

what.value: Maximum value of CO(13-12) scaled to CO(10-9) as upper limits for LVG modeling, and local ULIRG CO SLEDs

evidence.quote: To constrain the *2-component* model, which has more free parameters than *1-component* and *Turbulence*, we consider the maximum value of CO(13$-$12) from (cite: rosenberg15) scaled to $\rm CO(10-9)$ in W and E as upper limits.
The local ULIRGs sample includes 29 galaxies taken from (cite: rosenberg15), excluding NGC 6240 which is an outlier due to galaxy wide shocks (cite: meijerink13).

what.value: Local and high-redshift galaxy continuum photometry and H2O luminosities for L_H2O - L_FIR correlation

evidence.quote: In case of the local galaxies, the continuum flux density values are from (cite: sanders03) and $\rm L_{H_{2}O}$ from (cite: yang13).
The photometry and magnification in the high-redshift galaxies are from (cite: weiss07; riechers09; riechers13; bussmann13; cooray14) and $\rm L_{H_{2}O}$ from (cite: omont13; yang16).

external_data.citation: (cite: sanders03; yang13; weiss07; riechers09; riechers13; bussmann13; cooray14; omont13; yang16; apostolovski19)

what.value: Main sequence, high-redshift SMG, and SPT-SMG samples for alpha_CO and depletion time comparisons

evidence.quote: The main sequence galaxy (MS) sample is taken from (cite: magnelli12), the high-redshift SMGs from (cite: carilli10; walter12; fu12; ivison13; fu13; alaghbandzadeh13), and the SPT-SMG sample is from (cite: aravena16) and (cite: reuter20).

recipe.goal: Image continuum and spectral lines and extract 1D spectra
recipe.method: Image continuum by combining LSB and USB excluding line channels; subtract continuum in uv-plane using uvcontsub (order 1); image spectral cubes at 100 km/s resolution and single-channel moment 0 maps; extract 1D spectra using apertures of 2.5'' (W) and 1.2'' (E).
key_parameters: Spectral cube velocity averaging = 100 km s^-1; Moment 0 single channel width = 1000 km s^-1 (W) and 500 km s^-1 (E)
assumptions: Velocity separation of ~750 km s^-1 between W and E based on [CII] observations

recipe.goal: Decompose blended and non-Gaussian spectral lines and calculate line luminosities
recipe.method: Re-image ALMA 240 GHz [CII] data with the same weighting and velocity averaging to use as a high-SNR template; scale the [CII] template to observed line spectra (jointly for blended lines) via least squares; integrate flux from line center - 3*sigma_v to + 3*sigma_v; repeat 3000 times with random Gaussian noise to get median and standard deviation; convert I_obs to L_line and L'_line using Solomon et al. (1997) equations.
key_parameters: [CII] template FWHM = 779 +/- 25 km s^-1 (W) and 371 +/- 12 km s^-1 (E)
Integration range: line center - 3*sigma_v to line center + 3*sigma_v; 3000 Monte Carlo iterations
assumptions: Molecular lines share the same kinematic profile as the [CII] template; unresolved ATCA CO(3-2) flux distributed between W and E by scaling to CO(6-5); flat LambdaCDM cosmology (h = 0.677, Omega_m = 0.307, Omega_Lambda = 0.693)

recipe.goal: Perform gravitational lens modeling in the visibility plane
recipe.method: Fit parametric lens models to visibility data of 140 GHz and 101 GHz continuum and single-channel (1000 km/s) CO(6-5), CO(7-6), and CO(10-9) lines in W using visilens with SIE lens profile and Sersic source profile(s).
key_parameters: 1000 MCMC chains; lens parameters constrained within best-fit values of 140 GHz single-lens model
assumptions: SIE lens mass profile, Sersic source profile; fixed magnification mu = 1.3 for E and mu = 2.2 for p-H2O in W from Marrone et al. (2018)

recipe.goal: Fit modified blackbody dust SED to derive dust temperature, dust mass, L_FIR, and L_IR
recipe.method: Fit a uniform-temperature modified blackbody function (including CMB effect) to magnification-corrected rest-frame >50 um photometry using MCMC to sample M_dust and T_dust, then integrate rest-frame 8-1000 um for L_IR and 42.5-122.5 um for L_FIR.
key_parameters: 15% calibration/lensing error added in quadrature; upper limit on effective radius = 5000 pc (W) and 1300 pc (E)
assumptions: Uniform dust temperature; kappa_nu = 0.038 * (nu / 372.7 GHz)^beta_Td [m^2 kg^-1] from Draine (2003); beta_Td fixed to 2.0

recipe.goal: Analyze L_H2O - L_FIR correlation and derive H2O-based SFR and [CI]-based gas mass
recipe.method: Perform MCMC linear regression of log10(L_H2O/L_FIR) vs log10(L_FIR) across SPT0311-58 and literature sample; calibrate Kennicutt & Evans (2012) SFR relation with L_H2O; calculate molecular gas mass from [CI](2-1) luminosity using Weiss et al. (2003, 2005) equation with CMB correction.
assumptions: No differential magnification between H2O and continuum; SFR [M_sun/yr] = 1.47e-10 L_IR [L_sun]; T_ex = 30 K for [CI]; [CI]/[H2] = (8.4 +/- 3.5)e-5; Helium correction factor = 1.36

recipe.goal: Perform non-LTE LVG radiative transfer modeling of dust, CO, and [CI] simultaneously
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit dust continuum, CO SLED, and [CI](2-1) flux densities using non-LTE LVG radiative transfer models (1-component, 2-component, and Turbulence models, where Turbulence samples 50 densities from a log-normal PDF) optimized via the Monte Carlo Bees Algorithm.
key_parameters: 10 input parameters (1-component), 20 input parameters (2-component), 12 input parameters (Turbulence); 30 independent runs evaluating ~10^7 models total

Parameter priors/ranges in Table 3: log(n_H2) in [1, 7], T_K in [21, 600] K, T_K/T_dust in [0.5, 6.0], beta_TK in [-0.5, -0.05], beta_Tdust in [1.5, 2.0], R_eff in [0.1, 5000] pc, kappa_vir in [1, 3], dv_turb in [5, 200] km/s, GDMR in [90, 1100] (or [120, 150] for Z_sun), [CO/H2] in [1e-7, 2e-4] (or [1e-4, 2e-4] for Z_sun), [CI/H2] in [1e-7, 1e-4], beta_[CI] in [-5, 0]
assumptions: Dust opacity kappa_nu / m^2 kg^-1 = 0.04 * (nu / 250 GHz)^beta_Td; log-normal density PDF in supersonically isothermal turbulent gas; T_K and [CI] abundance coupled to density as power laws in Turbulence model; Helium factor 1.36

recipe.goal: Derive alpha_CO, gas depletion timescales, and neutral gas energy budget
recipe.method: Calculate alpha_CO = M_gas / L'_CO(1-0) using LVG model L'_CO(1-0) and three M_gas estimates (LVG, dust mass with GDMR=100, and [CI](2-1)); test alpha_CO vs T_dust correlation via MCMC linear fit and F-test; compute t_dep = M_gas / SFR; compare integrated CO cooling energy over t_dep with turbulent kinetic energy and stellar wind/supernova feedback energy.
key_parameters: F-test p-value < 0.05 for alpha_CO vs T_dust slope
assumptions: GDMR = 100 for dust-based M_gas; Kroupa IMF with 0.2% O-type stars (10^49-51 erg over 5 Myr) and 7% supernova progenitors (10-40 M_sun, 10^51 erg each, <=1% efficiency to turbulence)
